hypothesis: Add one bounded task-local graph-equivalent augmented-memory mechanism: retain the highest-scoring unique oracle-evaluated molecular graphs and, on later updates, replay a small historical elite set together with the unchanged current elite set through several distinct randomized SMILES traversals of each graph, applying its already observed reward to every equivalent traversal while averaging the loss within each graph.
method_thesis: Train a task-agnostic autoregressive SMILES model only on the allowed unlabeled corpus, freeze a copy as the prior, and restart a trainable agent for each independent objective session. Generate the first proposals ancestrally, then use returned oracle scores to apply top-fraction prior-regularized likelihood updates to the agent. Whenever the recent reward trajectory shows sustained improvement, run Beam Enumeration on the current agent without calling the oracle: expand its most probable partial token trajectories, convert chemically interpretable partial strings into connected molecular substructures, and retain a small task-local pool of recurrent motifs. Fill subsequent evaluator-announced batches by sampling complete SMILES de novo from the agent and locally rejecting any valid novel sample that lacks every pooled motif; canonicalize and remove already evaluated or within-batch duplicates before submission. The enumerated objects are transient partial token trajectories, not whole candidate molecules, and neither they nor any corpus molecule are scored, ranked, retrieved, or submitted as a finite library. Thus oracle feedback changes both the policy and a dynamic structural gate on fresh generation, concentrating the 290 adaptive calls on chemistry expressed by successful policy updates while the only success criterion remains the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores.

method_tags.learning_mechanism: offline corpus language-model training plus task-local top-fraction prior-regularized likelihood updates from current oracle feedback
method_tags.proposal_mechanism: dynamic top-probability beam expansion for motif extraction followed by motif-gated rejection sampling of complete de novo SMILES
method_tags.representation: tokenized SMILES plus RDKit-extracted connected substructures from partial token trajectories

applicability_conditions: Task-local oracle scores remain valid across rounds, so a stored reward can supervise later representations of the same molecular graph.

High-reward graphs admit more than one distinct randomized SMILES that is representable by the fixed vocabulary; highly symmetric graphs or vocabulary rejection may reduce augmentation to the bounded observed-trajectory fallback and weaken the mechanism.

Graph-equivalent token diversity exposes shared chemical structure without overwhelming the frozen corpus prior; averaging within graph is required so graphs with more available traversals do not receive more objective weight.

A five-graph historical contribution and a 50-graph memory remain small enough that current elites and ancestral novelty are preserved; transfer is weaker when repeated high-reward graphs collapse sequence diversity or when the optimum is disconnected from memory chemistry.

The mechanism is intended for a sequence policy whose downstream beam motifs are sensitive to token serialization. It may not help if motif failure is caused instead by genuinely absent graph support or by generic but parseable motifs.

Node n-414fec57359e establishes that exact historical replay can activate yet remain score-negative on its different Parent; it does not settle this graph-equivalent claim because this mechanism changes the unit of supervision from one stored token path to an equal-weight molecular graph represented by several randomized paths, on top of n-96c750192e04's beam-gated Parent stack.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not happen if eligible later updates contain no uniquely traceable graph created in an earlier round, if any retained randomized SMILES fails to canonicalize to its recorded source graph or is sent to the oracle, if multi-serialization coverage remains at the Parent's zero reference despite eligible graphs, or if the aggregate paired length-normalized reward-target gap on the non-original randomized trajectories does not decrease after optimization.
research_intent.implementation_change: Keep corpus preparation, model architecture, ancestral proposal sampling, oracle interaction, current-batch top-half selection, reward scale, optimizer settings, sustained-improvement trigger, Beam Enumeration, motif extraction, gating, canonicalization, and duplicate rejection unchanged. Add a deterministic task-local memory capped at 50 unique canonical molecules, storing each accepted sampled trajectory, score, and creation round; before inserting the current feedback, select up to the five highest-scoring entries created in earlier rounds and combine them with the five current elites. For every selected graph, retain its observed trajectory and attempt at most 16 seeded RDKit random traversals to obtain up to three additional distinct, tokenizable SMILES that canonicalize back to that same graph, with the observed trajectory as the bounded valid fallback. Compute the existing frozen-prior-plus-scaled-reward target separately for every representation, average squared target-gap loss across representations within a graph and then equally across selected graphs, and run the unchanged two optimizer steps. Insert the current accepted graphs and deterministically trim the memory only after the update, so historical membership is strict and no augmented representation is submitted to the oracle.
research_intent.mechanism: Add one bounded task-local graph-equivalent augmented-memory mechanism: retain the highest-scoring unique oracle-evaluated molecular graphs and, on later updates, replay a small historical elite set together with the unchanged current elite set through several distinct randomized SMILES traversals of each graph, applying its already observed reward to every equivalent traversal while averaging the loss within each graph.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: Parent n-96c750192e04 uses each accepted molecular reward only once and only through the exact sampled SMILES trajectory from the current batch: all 145 updates had zero replay, and 76 of 725 selected trajectories failed to move closer to their reward-augmented targets. That trajectory-specific reward use is especially limiting for structural self-conditioning because median_2 produced no recurrent motif on its final five beam refreshes and finished at 0.20178594524812024, while sitagliptin_mpo had the weakest elite movement at 103 of 145 trajectories and finished at 0.20558906877196068. Merely repeating exact strings is not enough evidence for the desired invariance: n-414fec57359e successfully replayed 700 historical trajectories and reduced their aggregate target gap, but its seed-0 macro score was 0.045374913404951034 below its anchor and sitagliptin_mpo showed a gap decrease on only 14 of 28 eligible updates. The limiting behaviour is therefore that one graph-level reward remains tied to one transient token serialization instead of persistently shaping multiple equivalent SMILES trajectories.

applicability_conditions: Task-local reward reuse is supported across all three Search Seeds for these stationary sessions: every one of 2,100 historical graph selections resolves to an earlier accepted evaluator trajectory from the same seed and task with exact canonical identity, creation round, and stored score, and all 15 task sessions start with empty memory.

Representational diversity is strongly supported on the observed chemistry and fixed vocabulary: all 4,275 selected graphs retain multiple distinct tokenizations, 4,274 retain three randomized traversals in addition to the observed path, and the one long-graph exception retains two randomized traversals. All 17,099 retained paths round-trip exactly.

Equal graph supervision operated as intended: 4,274 four-representation groups use within-graph weight 0.25, the single three-representation group uses weight one third, every graph receives equal update weight, graph identities are unique within each update, and every representation shares its graph's stored reward.

The bounded-memory regime is supported for batch size 10 and 29 adaptive rounds: all 420 eligible updates select exactly five strict-prior-round graphs, memory remains task-local and never exceeds 50 unique canonical graphs, every announced batch fills, and no augmented path is submitted to the oracle.

The intermediate effect is reproducible under this implementation: the aggregate randomized gap decreases on each of seeds 0, 1, and 2 and in every one of the 15 seed-task pools. Transfer beyond these tasks is weaker when long or symmetric molecules reduce usable randomized paths, when the optimum is disconnected from memory chemistry, or when a narrow elite memory suppresses proposal diversity.

The supported behavioural claim remains reward-target contraction in this sequence policy. The logs do not directly establish that graph-equivalent replay improves the causal usefulness of beam-derived motifs; applicability is weaker when downstream motif failure reflects absent graph support or generic but parseable motifs rather than token-serialization sensitivity.

The bound algorithmic Parent n-96c750192e04 registers no randomized or historical optimizer trajectory, so the preregistered randomized-SMILES and historical-graph paired gaps are absent at its zero-coverage reference.
observable_measurements.value: The predicted aggregate contraction replicates independently. On seed 1, the 4,274 non-original randomized representations decrease in pooled absolute length-normalized target gap from 0.1689112877303509 to 0.13393985347801196, a paired change of -0.03497143425233895, with 3,312/4,274 individual representations and 137/145 update-level randomized means moving closer. On seed 2, the 4,275 randomized representations decrease from 0.2174928896186658 to 0.18092528347922907, a paired change of -0.03656760613943674, with 3,287/4,275 individual representations and 137/145 update means moving closer. Across all three seeds, 12,824 randomized representations decrease from 0.1941777832586367 to 0.15671163727507517, a paired change of -0.037466145983561516; 9,939/12,824 individual representations and 413/435 update means move closer, and the pooled randomized mean decreases in all 15 seed-task groups. The 2,175 original current trajectories separately decrease from 0.25384564639984125 to 0.242422631173786, a paired change of -0.011423015226055239, with 1,707/2,175 moving closer. Equal-within-graph aggregation decreases across all 4,275 graph means from 0.21961596324689442 to 0.18766630052354688, a paired change of -0.03194966272334754; on the 2,100 historical graph means specifically it decreases from 0.238463276320891 to 0.20385959426251551, a paired change of -0.034603682058375496, with 1,887/2,100 historical graphs moving closer. Every retained representation exposes prior, pre-update agent, post-update agent, token-count, reward, and target values; the largest absolute residual from frozen-prior likelihood plus 60 times stored reward is 1.3762539879280666e-05 under the logged float32 calculation. Thus contraction occurs on non-original randomized and historical graph supervision, not only on exact current strings.

possible_failure_causes: Contraction is aggregate rather than universal. Across the three seeds, 2,885/12,824 non-original randomized representations do not move closer to target and 22/435 update-level randomized means do not decrease (six on seed 0 and eight on each replication seed). Shared-parameter interference and two-step overshoot can oppose individual serialization targets even though every seed's pooled effect decreases.

Historical replay is also nonuniform: 213/2,100 equal-within-graph historical gaps do not decrease, and 16/420 eligible update-level historical means do not decrease. The mechanism therefore supplies repeatable aggregate contraction, not a guarantee for every stored graph or policy state.

Bounded augmentation encountered a concrete length limit on seed-1 drd2_docking: one long current graph retained only two randomized traversals because 14 of its bounded attempts exceeded the maximum token length. The other 73 rejected attempts across all seeds were duplicate representations. More long, symmetric, or vocabulary-incompatible graphs could exhaust the 16-attempt bound more often and weaken token-serialization diversity.

Five historical graphs and five current elites each receive half of the equal-graph objective weight on eligible rounds. A stale or chemically narrow high-score memory could reduce immediate current-batch plasticity, reinforce a repeated neighborhood, or perturb later beam motifs even when replay provenance and target contraction are correct.

The evidence isolates execution and reward-target contraction, not the separate causal contributions of historical memory and randomized serialization, nor whether either improves motif usefulness, motif persistence, or terminal benchmark score. Replication now covers all three Search Seeds but remains limited to the fixed Hard-Five tasks, vocabulary, update schedule, and oracle budget.

Equal graph supervision operated as intended: every four-representation group used within-graph weight 0.25, each selected graph had equal update weight, canonical graph identities were unique within every optimizer update, and all representation copies shared the graph's stored reward.

The bounded-memory regime is supported for batch size 10 and 29 adaptive rounds: all 140 eligible updates selected exactly five strict prior-round graphs, memory remained task-local and at most 50 unique canonical graphs, every announced batch filled, and no augmented path entered evaluator trajectories.

possible_failure_causes: Contraction is aggregate rather than universal. Of 4,275 non-original randomized trajectories, 935 did not move closer to target; six of 145 update-level randomized means increased, comprising five sitagliptin_mpo updates and one zaleplon_mpo update. Shared-parameter interference and two-step overshoot can therefore oppose individual serialization targets even though the pooled effect is a decrease.

Historical replay is also nonuniform: 74/700 equal-within-graph historical gaps did not decrease. Sitagliptin_mpo is the weakest task-level case, with randomized-gap decrease on only 24/29 updates and historical-graph contraction on 109/140 graphs, so serialization invariance may be less reliable for some objective-conditioned policy states.

The observed chemistry yielded three retained randomized traversals for every selected graph, but 10 duplicate traversals already required extra attempts. More symmetric graphs, longer strings, or vocabulary-incompatible randomized forms could exhaust the 16-attempt bound and collapse some graphs to the observed-trajectory fallback, weakening the graph-equivalent training signal.

On eligible rounds the five historical graphs and five current elites each receive half of the total equal-graph objective weight. A stale or chemically narrow high-score memory can therefore reduce immediate current-batch plasticity, reinforce repeated neighborhoods, or alter the downstream beam motif pool even when all replay provenance is correct.

Only screening seed 0 was evaluated. The evidence proves execution and predicted intermediate contraction, but it does not isolate whether memory, randomized serialization, or their interaction caused terminal score movement, nor whether the changed policy improves beam-motif quality or remains stable over additional seeds.

applicability_conditions: Task-local oracle scores remain valid across rounds, so a stored reward can supervise later representations of the same molecular graph.

High-reward graphs admit more than one distinct randomized SMILES that is representable by the fixed vocabulary; highly symmetric graphs or vocabulary rejection may reduce augmentation to the bounded observed-trajectory fallback and weaken the mechanism.

Graph-equivalent token diversity exposes shared chemical structure without overwhelming the frozen corpus prior; averaging within graph is required so graphs with more available traversals do not receive more objective weight.

A five-graph historical contribution and a 50-graph memory remain small enough that current elites and ancestral novelty are preserved; transfer is weaker when repeated high-reward graphs collapse sequence diversity or when the optimum is disconnected from memory chemistry.

The mechanism is intended for a sequence policy whose downstream beam motifs are sensitive to token serialization. It may not help if motif failure is caused instead by genuinely absent graph support or by generic but parseable motifs.

Node n-414fec57359e establishes that exact historical replay can activate yet remain score-negative on its different Parent; it does not settle this graph-equivalent claim because this mechanism changes the unit of supervision from one stored token path to an equal-weight molecular graph represented by several randomized paths, on top of n-96c750192e04's beam-gated Parent stack.
